blocks.text: Condo buildings in East Cambie
Streets, schools and getting around East Cambie

items.t: East Cambie is in the City of Richmond, on the east side of the city, abutting the Agricultural Land Reserve along No. 6 Road and Westminster Highway; it is an official City planning area (the East Cambie Area Plan, Schedule 2.11B to the Official Community Plan). The Area Plan's boundary maps are graphics whose roads are not stated in the plan text, so a full text boundary is UNVERIFIED; City data sheets confirm Cambie Road addresses are in the East Cambie Planning Area.

Main roads named in the plan: Cambie Road, No. 5 Road and Westminster Highway, with Highway 91 (the Richmond Freeway) and the Alex Fraser Bridge (named "Annacis Bridge" in the plan text) giving the area its cross-river access. West Cambie is to the west, Bridgeport to the north-west, and ALR farmland runs along the No. 6 Road and Westminster Highway edges.

Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere, in apartment form —. The documented base form is single detached housing; the Area Plan anticipated residential projects along some major roads at townhouse or apartment densities, and the built strata product that has actually been verified in this area is townhouse form on and near the Cambie Road / No. 5 Road corridors.

The commercial node is the south-west corner of Cambie Road and No. 5 Road — the Area Plan names it the principal community commercial area (Cambie Plaza), with the Richmond Auto Mall as an existing smaller commercial centre; Richmond Public Library's Cambie Branch is at 150-11590 Cambie Road in that node and Cambie Community Centre is at 12800 Cambie Road.

Transit: the one timetable service confirmed in the research pass is the TransLink 430 Express stopping on Garden City Road at Cambie Road at the area's west edge, running between Richmond-Brighouse Station and Metrotown Station; the full list of bus routes on Cambie Road and No. 5 Road is UNVERIFIED — do not promise specific Cambie Road routes the timetables do not support.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in East Cambie

items.t: Richmond zoning and plans: the area's base zone is Single Detached (RS1/RS2) under Zoning Bylaw No. 8500 — the RS1/E subzone documented on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot area of 550.0 m², minimum width 18.0 m and minimum depth 24.0 m, with one principal dwelling per lot and a secondary suite as a permitted secondary use. The East Cambie Area Plan is Schedule 2.11B to the Official Community Plan (adopted October 21, 2002; Land Use Map updated by Bylaw 9874) under the city-wide 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000; the City began a further OCP update process in fall 2024 toward a 2050 horizon. In East Cambie, multiple-family sites are Development Permit Areas under the Area Plan.

Suites / SSMUH: the City states it allows at least one secondary suite and/or accessory dwelling unit per lot on covered lots, with Bill 44 small-scale multi-unit minimums of 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on larger lots.

Flood rules — the Richmond-specific diligence item: all lands within Richmond are designated flood plain under Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw No. 8204, which sets flood construction levels (FCLs) that habitable floors must meet unless an exemption applies; Richmond sits at an average of 1 metre above sea level behind 49 km of dikes designed for a 1:500 flood event, with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres under way, and the Area Plan requires new development in East Cambie to provide adequate flood protection. Strata insurance and FCL compliance are building-specific checks on any East Cambie strata purchase.

Richmond money dates: 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid taxes after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% penalty on any outstanding balance after Tuesday, September 1, 2026; annual flat-rate utility payments were due March 31, 2026, with a 10% discount only for payments received on or before the due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about East Cambie

items.t: The plan is older than the townhouses. The East Cambie Area Plan was adopted October 21, 2002 (Land Use Map updated by Bylaw 9874) and already anticipated corridor townhouse/apartment densities — Cambie Gardens (2005) and Wembley (2020) are that 2002 plan arriving, a generation apart. The City also began a further OCP update in fall 2024 toward a 2050 horizon, so the plan framework over any new strata here is mid-revision.

The area's biggest park is a bog inside the ALR. Richmond Nature Park, 11851 Westminster Highway, is 100+ acres of old bog forest with the Nature House interpretive centre, the Area Plan conserves it as a bog environment, and the plan also protects Bath Slough as a natural watercourse — the "green edge" beside the townhouse corridors is protected bog, not future development land.

Mitchell Elementary carries a heritage ask. The Area Plan asks the School Board to conserve the Mitchell School buildings as heritage structures, and Mitchell is the longest continuously operating school in the Richmond public system, named after Richmond pioneer Alex Mitchell — relevant context for any redevelopment expectation near the Cambie / No. 5 node.

King George / Cambie Community Park is the plan's anchor park. At 4100 No. 5 Road, with heritage trees, courts, playgrounds, tennis and a waterpark, the Area Plan calls it the principal community park, to be retained and expanded on its present site — the amenity the Thorpe Road and No. 5 Road townhouse stock actually lives beside.

The bridge in the plan has two names. The Area Plan text calls the Alex Fraser Bridge the "Annacis Bridge" — older planning documents, listing copy and local speech for this area use both names for the same Highway 91 crossing that gives East Cambie its Delta and Surrey access.

items.t: Where the townhouse stock concentrates: (1) the Cambie Road corridor west of No. 5 Road — Cambie Gardens, Cambie Court; (2) the McNeely Drive / Jack Bell Drive pocket south of Cambie Road — Sausalito, Francisco Village, Capistrano, Malibu, Normandie on Thorpe Road; (3) the No. 5 Road / Highway 91 node — Wembley. The documented base form is otherwise single detached housing; the Area Plan anticipated residential projects along some major roads at townhouse or apartment densities.

Schools: SD38 (Richmond) runs K–7 elementary and 8–12 secondary with no middle-school tier. Schools physically in the area: Mitchell Elementary, 3800 No. 5 Road; Kathleen McNeely Elementary, 12440 Woodhead Road; and H.J. Cambie Secondary, 4151 Jacombs Road. The SD38 locator result for the sample address 11671 Cambie Road is Mitchell Elementary and Cambie Secondary — catchments are address-based.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in East Cambie

items.t: Form B diligence (all 8 strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For a 13-unit complex like Cambie Gardens, the Form B is effectively the whole financial picture. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

Richmond zoning and plans: Zoning Bylaw 8500 governs — the area's base zone is Single Detached (RS1/RS2) under Section 8.1, and the RS1/E subzone documented on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot area of 550.0 m², minimum width 18.0 m and minimum depth 24.0 m, with one principal dwelling per lot and a secondary suite as a permitted secondary use. Townhouse sites proceed under low-density townhouse zones (the RTL4 rezoning record in is the worked example) and multiple-family sites are Development Permit Areas under the Area Plan. The East Cambie Area Plan is Schedule 2.11B to the Official Community Plan (adopted October 21, 2002; Land Use Map updated by Bylaw 9874) under the city-wide 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000.

Flood — the Richmond-specific diligence item: all lands within Richmond are designated flood plain under Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw No. 8204, which sets flood construction levels (FCLs) that habitable floors must meet unless an exemption applies; Richmond sits at an average of 1 metre above sea level behind 49 km of dikes designed for a 1:500 flood event, with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres under way, and the Area Plan requires new development in East Cambie to provide adequate flood protection. Strata insurance and FCL compliance are building-specific checks on any East Cambie strata purchase.

blocks.text: Lots and land in East Cambie
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established-street house lots: single detached housing is the documented base form — a City data sheet for 11671 and 11691 Cambie Road gives the existing zoning as Single Detached (RS1/E) under an OCP designation of Neighbourhood Residential — and the Area Plan states residential projects were anticipated along some major roads at townhouse or apartment densities.

Lot character from the zone, as the research states it: the RS1/E subzone documented on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot area of 550.0 m², minimum width 18.0 m and minimum depth 24.0 m under Zoning Bylaw 8500, Section 8.1 (RS1/RS2), with one principal dwelling per lot and a secondary suite as a permitted secondary use. These are zone figures for that subzone, not a claim about any existing lot's size; other subzones apply elsewhere in the area and are confirmed with the City.

Serviced position, as the sources state it: septic / well status is UNVERIFIED in the research; the Area Plan refers to sanitary and storm sewer upgrades in older subdivisions — servicing history therefore varies by subdivision pocket, and servicing for any single lot is confirmed with the City, UNCONFIRMED parcel-by-parcel here.

ALR vs non-ALR split, as the plan states it: the East Cambie Planning Area abuts the Agricultural Land Reserve along No. 6 Road and Westminster Highway, the Richmond Nature Park is within the ALR, and a plan goal is a distinct boundary between agricultural and non-agricultural lands. The ALR ground is therefore at the area's east and Westminster Highway edges, not interleaved through the residential streets on this evidence; no lot-count or percentage split is stated, and a specific property's ALR status is a per-address check on Agricultural Land Commission maps.

Flood position — citywide, no exceptions on this evidence: Richmond is made up of islands within the floodplain of the Fraser River at an average of 1 metre above sea level, behind a flood protection system of 49 km of dikes designed for a 1:500 event (0.2% chance in any year), with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres under way; all lands within Richmond are designated flood plain under Bylaw No. 8204, and the Area Plan says new development in East Cambie is to provide adequate flood protection.
Market context: Any East Cambie median quoted elsewhere is UNVERIFIED for the purposes of these notes.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in East Cambie

items.t: Plan: the East Cambie Area Plan is Schedule 2.11B to the Official Community Plan (plan adoption October 21, 2002; Land Use Map updated by Bylaw 9874), under the city-wide 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000 (Schedule 1); the City began a further OCP update process in fall 2024 toward a 2050 horizon.

SSMUH / suites as the City states them: the City states it allows at least one secondary suite and/or accessory dwelling unit per lot on covered lots, with Bill 44 small-scale multi-unit minimums of 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on larger lots.

ALR rules (the area genuinely abuts ALR ground, so these bite at the edges): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

Heritage note for lot diligence near the node: the Area Plan asks the School Board to conserve the Mitchell School buildings as heritage structures, and Mitchell Elementary is the longest continuously operating school in the Richmond public system — relevant context for redevelopment expectations near the Cambie Road / No. 5 Road node, not a lot rule.

Richmond property taxes and utilities: 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid taxes after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% penalty on any outstanding balance after Tuesday, September 1, 2026; annual flat-rate utility payments were due March 31, 2026, with a 10% discount only for payments received on or before the due date, and the City's typical single-family metered utility total for 2026 is $2,251 per year (water $631, sewer $835, garbage/recycling/environmental programs $443, flood protection $342).

The bridge in the plan has two names: the Area Plan text calls the Alex Fraser Bridge the "Annacis Bridge" — older planning documents, listing copy and local speech for this area use both names for the same Highway 91 crossing that gives East Cambie its Delta and Surrey access.

King George / Cambie Community Park is the plan's anchor park: at 4100 No. 5 Road, with heritage trees, courts, playgrounds, tennis and a waterpark, the Area Plan calls it the principal community park, to be retained and expanded on its present site — amenity value that attaches to the surrounding house lots, not development land.
Cambie Secondary — the assignment was fixed to Vancouver and must never be re-filed here; East Cambie's secondary school is H.J. Cambie Secondary, 4151 Jacombs Road.

faq.q: Which schools are in East Cambie?
faq.a: Mitchell Elementary at 3800 No. 5 Road, Kathleen McNeely Elementary at 12440 Woodhead Road and H.J. Cambie Secondary at 4151 Jacombs Road are physically in the area; for the sample address used (11671 Cambie Road), the SD38 locator gives Mitchell Elementary and Cambie Secondary — catchments for other addresses must be checked in the locator.

faq.q: Are suites and added units allowed on single detached lots here?
faq.a: The RS1/RS2 zone lists a secondary suite as a secondary use, and the City states it allows at least one secondary suite and/or accessory dwelling unit per lot, with Bill 44 small-scale multi-unit minimums of 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on larger lots.

faq.q: Does the Agricultural Land Reserve touch East Cambie?
faq.a: Yes — the Area Plan states the planning area abuts the ALR along No. 6 Road and Westminster Highway, and the Richmond Nature Park is within the ALR.

faq.q: Can Jared show me homes in East Cambie?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Are there any apartment condos in East Cambie?
faq.a: None verified. The strata product that exists here is townhouse form (Cambie Gardens, Wembley, the Thorpe Road complex).

faq.q: So what strata can I actually buy in East Cambie?
faq.a: Townhouses: Cambie Gardens (11331 Cambie Road, 13 duplex-style townhomes, built 2005) and Wembley (4991 No.

faq.q: Will apartment condos ever be built here?
faq.a: The Area Plan anticipates townhouse or apartment densities along some major roads, multiple-family sites are Development Permit Areas under the plan, and a City application already documents an RS1/E-to-RTL4 townhouse rezoning at 11671/11691 Cambie Road — the direction is corridor strata, townhouse first. No current apartment presale in the area was verified.

faq.q: Does flood risk affect a strata purchase here?
faq.a: Yes, structurally: all of Richmond is designated flood plain under Bylaw No. 8204 with flood construction levels for habitable floors, and strata insurance pricing in Richmond reflects the dike-and-floodplain setting (49 km of dikes, 1:500 design event, dike raising to 4.7 m under way). Ask for the building's FCL compliance and insurance terms rather than assuming from the map.

faq.q: Which schools serve an East Cambie townhouse?
faq.a: Schools physically in the area: Mitchell Elementary (3800 No. 5 Road), Kathleen McNeely Elementary (12440 Woodhead Road) and H.J. Cambie Secondary (4151 Jacombs Road); SD38 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12). The verified locator result, for the sample address 11671 Cambie Road, is Mitchell Elementary and Cambie Secondary — but McNeely also sits inside the area, so run every address in the SD38 locator. King George Secondary is a Vancouver (SD39) school and has no bearing here, despite a past filing error.

faq.q: What strata can I actually buy in East Cambie?
faq.a: Townhouses: eight verified strata complexes — Cambie Gardens (11331 Cambie Road, 13 duplex-style townhomes, built 2005), Wembley (4991 No. 5 Road, by Citimark, built 2020, 109 townhomes per the presale record), Normandie (11571 Thorpe Road, 77 units), Cambie Court (12311 Cambie Road), and the Polygon-era McNeely / Jack Bell pocket: Sausalito, Francisco Village, Capistrano and Malibu. No apartment condos and no fee-simple townhouse complex are verified in the area.

faq.q: Sausalito — is it 1993 or 1994, and does it matter?
faq.a: It matters only for warranty-era and depreciation-report expectations — the strata's own documents, not either published year, govern.

faq.q: Can I rent out an East Cambie townhouse?
faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022. Directory lines reading "rentals allowed with restrictions" (Sausalito, Capistrano) cannot restrict a long-term rental today; a short-term rental bylaw can still bind you — read the registered bylaws in the Form B package.
